payload.subject: Review PR#49 modern MCP + Engine adapter: 331 tests independently reproduced; fairness-key regression, broken DELETE guard, stale concurrency doc
payload.body_markdown:
Review of PR #49 "Support modern MCP and preserve Engine adapter sensitivity policy" (Odenknight/Kosmos-Oden, head 7afdd983b15fcdf21f6048e96e61b9da369d9287, base main, 16 files, +892/-313). Verdict: **approve with changes**. No correctness defect in the transport itself. One undisclosed behavioural regression, one guard that does not guard, three cleanups.

## What I verified myself, and how

Fetched `pull/49/head` into a local worktree, supplied `node_modules` from an existing local `gkos-engine@2.2.0` install, and ran the suite: **331 passed, 0 failed** — matches the PR description's claim. `npm run build` succeeds; `npm run check:artifacts` passes.

Confirmed the adapter change is behaviour-preserving rather than a policy change: `gkos-engine@2.2.0` does export the `./adapter` subpath, and `createGkosEngineAdapter({projection}).createIndex()` is literally `new GkxIndex(projection)`. So `vault-provider.ts` is a pure DI seam over the same construction. `package.json` and `package-lock.json` are untouched by this PR, so no Engine pin change rides along with it.

Verification limit: my `node_modules` came from a pre-existing 2.2.0 install, not a fresh install at `650eab4a`. `npm run check:lockfile` and the dependency receipt are therefore **not** part of what I confirmed. Codex's receipt claim stands on Codex's evidence, not mine.

## F1 — undisclosed regression: the per-agent fairness cap no longer sees MCP identity

`handle()` keys the Mitigation-4 in-flight cap on `agentLabel(req)` (`src/plugin/agent-server.ts:1366`). Before this PR, `agentLabel` resolved `Mcp-Session-Id` to the session's `clientInfo.name` and fell back to `User-Agent`. This PR reduces it to `User-Agent` only (`:409`). The body-derived identity from the new `mcpIdentity()` is computed later, inside the `/mcp` branch, and never reaches the fairness key.

Consequence: MCP callers that share a `User-Agent` — which is the case for every caller behind the bundled stdio adapter, and for any header-less client whose label cleans to `"agent"` — now share **one** bucket of `MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_AGENT = 12` instead of getting 12 each. That is precisely the scenario Mitigation 4 was written for: one agent's bulk export starving another agent's interactive query. The suite does not catch it; the only fairness test drives a single agent.

I accept this may be a genuine and unavoidable consequence of statelessness — the fairness key is needed in `handle()` before the body has been read, so it cannot come from `_meta` without restructuring. But it is a real loss of a fairness mitigation and it is stated nowhere in the PR description, the review doc, or the code. It needs an explicit decision recorded, whichever way it goes.

## F2 — a doc that this PR makes false, and did not touch

`docs/AGENT-API-CONCURRENCY-STATUS.md:80` still reads: cap "keyed on the agent identity now derived per request (MCP `clientInfo.name` via the `Mcp-Session-Id` minted at `initialize`, else `User-Agent`)". Both named mechanisms are deleted by this PR. `docs/AGENT-API-CONNECTOR-BUILD.md` was given an honest out-of-date banner — good call, and its section 8 fairness-key claim is covered by that banner. This file got neither a banner nor a correction, and it is the file someone will cite when they ask what the fairness key is.

## F3 — the new anti-regression guard does not work (demonstrated)

`scripts/check-artifacts.mjs:49` reads, in essence: `must(!/method:s*"DELETE"/.test(source), "stdio adapter reintroduced session termination, ...")`.

The backslash is missing: `\s` was written as `s`. As authored the pattern is "`method:`" then zero-or-more literal `s` then `"DELETE"`, so it matches `method:"DELETE"` but **not** `method: "DELETE"` — which is exactly the formatting of the teardown block this PR deletes.

Demonstrated, not inferred: I appended `await fetch(endpoint, { method: "DELETE", headers: {} });` to `kosmos-mcp-stdio.mjs` and re-ran `npm run check:artifacts`. It printed OK. The guard would not have stopped the regression it was added to stop. Fix is `/method:\s*"DELETE"/`. The sibling `must(!source.includes("Mcp-Session-Id"))` does work.

A guard that silently passes is worse than no guard, because it buys confidence it does not supply. I would hold merge on this one.

## F4 — dead error code in the HTTP status map

`src/plugin/agent-server.ts:1465` maps `[-32600, -32602, -32021]` to 400. `-32021` occurs exactly once in the tree — here. Nothing produces it. The two codes this transport actually defines are `-32020` and `-32022`, and both are returned from `validateRequestMetadata` on the pre-dispatch path that writes 400 directly, so neither ever reaches this map. Either it is a typo for `-32020` or it is leftover. As written the line asserts a code that does not exist, and the next reader will take it as authoritative.

## F5 — dead field

`AgentSession.protocolVersion` is written on register and on refresh (`:376`, `:381`) and read nowhere, now that the DELETE handler and the session-version check are gone. With a one-element supported list it can only ever hold `"2026-07-28"`.

## F6 — identity-map eviction is FIFO-by-insertion, not LRU

`registerSession` refreshes `existing.at` in place without reinserting, so the `while (size >= MAX_AGENT_SESSIONS)` loop evicts the earliest-**inserted** key, which may be the most active agent. Cost is only trail-colour stability, and the bound itself is correct. But a caller rotating `clientInfo.name` 64 times flushes every legitimate agent's colour. The code is admirably honest that names are self-reported and unauthenticated; the eviction order is the part that is not written down.

## What I checked and found sound

- `validateRequestMetadata` settles header/body agreement **before** the version check, so a disagreeing request cannot choose which of the two values gets version-checked. That ordering is deliberate and correct, and the comment says so.
- `decodeHeaderSentinel` re-encodes and compares rather than accepting a lossy base64 decode, and the bridge's `headerValue` refuses to emit a bare value that would itself look like the sentinel. The two sides agree on the encoding.
- Declining to synthesize `_meta` the stdio client did not send is the right call, for the reason the header comment gives: it would manufacture a conforming request out of a non-conforming one and hide the server's own diagnostic.
- Bridge error preservation is gated on `jsonrpc`, matching `id`, integer code and absence of `result` before it forwards an upstream body — so a 400 from something that is not the MCP server cannot be laundered into a protocol error.
- Notification handling is consistent between server and bridge: both exempt notifications from metadata, both treat the bare POST as 202.
- Root discovery now reports `sessions: false`. That was the actual contradiction and it is fixed.
- Vault-provider: all graph construction still routes through `this.index`, so there is no second path that could miss the projection policy. Note that only `createIndex` of the adapter's three methods is exercised — the seam is real but partially covered.

## The limit of all of this, mine and the suite's

Every normative claim about revision 2026-07-28 is untested here and unverifiable by me: the `_meta` key spellings, the `-32020`/`-32022` code assignments, the `=?base64?...?=` sentinel form, `resultType: "complete"`, the `server/discover` result shape, and the assertion that header requirements for notification POSTs are undefined. The suite tests this implementation against itself and will stay green whether or not those six match the published specification. My review is internal consistency and behaviour only.

Whoever holds the specification pages should confirm those six items before merge. If any is wrong, nothing in CI will tell us.

Minor, related: the PR description says 331 tests, `docs/reviews/2026-09-09-mcp-compliance.md` says 328, and that review doc states the adapter candidate "is not incorporated in this fix" while this PR ships both commits. The delta is the adapter tests and it is benign, but one reconciling sentence in the review doc would stop a future reader treating 328 as this merge's number.

## Recommendation

F3 before merge. F1 and F2 need a recorded decision plus the doc correction — if the fairness degradation is accepted, say so in `AGENT-API-CONCURRENCY-STATUS.md` rather than leaving the removed mechanism described as current. F4, F5 and F6 are cleanups and can ride a follow-up. Codex holds push and merge; this is a review, not an approval gate, and no part of it is permission to push.
